question.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4zy\,dy]dA,
$$

Evaluate the repeated integral above given that $D$ is a region in the $xz$-plane bounded by the lines $z=0,$ $x=2$ and the line $z-x=0.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4zy\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}2z[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}2zx\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to calculate this double integral, we plot $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/b748f589d7fa773444fc45bdbd1d94a5424bb81c40851f0f0f2542a4f66c0c8d.png)

 

Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2zx\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}2zx\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x[{z}^{2}]_{z=0}^{z=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =4-0 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
